pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: Family law runs on three clocks at once: the court's dates, the disclosure deadlines, and the client's money in trust. This workspace keeps all three on each matter so nobody has to remember them.
The four tables
Matters

: one row per case, with its stage (Intake, Retained, Disclosure, Mediation, Trial prep, Settled, Decree entered, Closed), the opposing party and counsel, court and case number, minor children and the fee arrangement. Each matter totals the assets and debts disclosed into a Net marital estate.
Clients
: the person you represent and the safe way to reach them. Safety concern means never leave a message at home and never send mail to a shared address.
Court dates and deadlines
: hearings, mediation sessions and filing or response deadlines. Write how the date was counted, so a second person can check it.
Financial disclosures
: every document either side owes: tax returns, statements, appraisals, debts, child expenses. Each has a category and a value once known.
A normal week
Monday: the paralegal opens Court dates and deadlines, This week view, and confirms each client knows their date.
Each new date is entered the day it is set, counted by one person and checked by another.
Disclosure requests are added from the matter with Request a document. Anything past due moves to Missing.
Friday: billing opens Matters and reads the Retainer check. Every Request top-up gets a letter.
Before any mediation, Documents outstanding on that matter must be zero or explained.

text.text: Most divorces settle on the numbers. Disclosure is where the numbers come from, and a missing statement is the usual reason a mediation day is wasted. This page is the routine the firm uses on every divorce and support matter.
Day one list
When a matter moves to Disclosure, add these from the matter with Request a document:

cells.text: Three years of tax returns, recent pay stubs, any bonus or commission letters
Twelve months of every checking, savings and brokerage account
Latest statements and the plan rules for any pension
Deed, mortgage statement, an appraisal or broker opinion
Two years of business returns, profit and loss, a valuation if contested
Card statements, car and equipment loans, tax debts
Childcare, school, activities and the children's health premium

text.text: Working the list
Set a due date on every request. Our client's documents are due in 21 days.
Other party's documents follow the rules or the standing order; write the deadline and how it was counted.
On arrival, check every page is there, then mark Received. After the attorney reviews it, enter its value and mark Reviewed.
Ours to produce: press Mark served when it goes to the other side.
Past due without a word: move to Missing and send the deficiency letter.
Reading the estate

The matter adds Assets disclosed and Debts disclosed into Net marital estate. It is only as good as the values entered. A retirement account still at zero means it has not been valued, not that it is empty.
Before mediation checklist
Documents outstanding is zero, or each missing item has a letter on file
Net marital estate reviewed with the client
Child support worked out on current income
Client's own list of the items they care most about

Family matters are long and unpredictable, so most hourly clients here sign an evergreen retainer: a deposit held in trust that is topped back up whenever it falls below an agreed floor. This page is how the firm keeps it fair to the client and safe for the firm.
How it works
The engagement letter names the deposit and the floor, for example a 7,500 deposit and a 5,000 floor.
Invoices are paid from trust only after the client has had the invoice for the agreed number of days.
When In trust now falls below Retainer floor, Retainer check says Request top-up.
Flat fee and limited scope matters say Not on retainer and are billed by their own letter.
Friday routine
Open Matters and the All matters view. Sort by Retainer check.
For each Request top-up, send the replenishment letter: the current balance, the floor, the amount needed and the date it is needed by.
Record the request date in the matter's page.
If a top-up is two weeks late and a hearing is close, the attorney calls the client before any more work is done.
Unbilled hours above 10 on a matter means invoices are due this week.
Words that help
"Your trust account is below the amount we agreed to keep on hand. A deposit of 2,100 by the 15th keeps your case moving without a pause before the mediation."
Plain numbers, a date, and the reason. Never surprise a client with a withdrawal.
Rules we never bend
Client money stays in trust until it is earned and invoiced.
One client's trust never pays another client's bill.
At close, any unused balance is refunded within 30 days, and the matter is closed with Close matter so the closing date is stamped.
Worked example

The Brennan matter has 1,900 in trust and a 3,500 floor before a half-day mediation. Billing sends the letter on Friday asking for 3,000; the client pays Tuesday, the balance is updated, and Retainer check returns to OK.
